outlook.statement: Strategic priorities: maximize operational efficiencies across sugar and bio-energy facilities; deepen ESG integration across all plant operations and supply chains; continue expanding into high-margin consumer and bio-fuel categories.
Company aims to expand ethanol production capacity from 65 KLPD to 85 KLPD by December 2027.

National imperative towards sustainable energy driven by Government's Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Program presents transformative opportunity; pivoting from traditional sugar manufacturer to integrated bio-energy and agribusiness solution provider.

Sugar production during Sugar Season (SS) 2026-27 is expected to recover by 3.6 million metric tonnes (raw value) to approximately 33.6 million metric tonnes, driven by consecutive favourable monsoon seasons, improved groundwater reserves, higher sugarcane yields and increased acreage under cultivation.

The comparative economics of ethanol versus sugar production remain critical for 2026/27 planning. Recent geopolitical tensions have elevated global oil prices to approximately $100 per barrel. The government was evaluating increased ethanol blending mandates to reduce petroleum import dependence and support domestic producer capacity.

Raw sugar prices currently trade sub 14 c/lb, which is below cost of production for most countries, including India. Any ethanol policy modifications could materially affect India's sugar output and global market equilibrium in 2026/27.

World sugar balance for 2025-26 would be turning to a surplus after six deficit years. Accordingly, world prices may be expected to remain range bound, barring unforeseen weather challenges in major producing centers. Southwest monsoon forecast for 2026 is below par compared to long period average. El-Nino challenge could be a major threat to cane crop in lead producing States like Maharashtra and Karnataka. Sugar production should still be more than adequate to take care of domestic demand, while GOI's decision on sugar exports and diversion for ethanol would hinge on crop assessment, post monsoon.

TN sugar industry continues to suffer in successive years in solitude. Water storage in State reservoirs are much below capacity and last year levels. It is facing an imminent survival challenge that cries for instant State intervention with imaginative and comprehensive package support measures for its resurrection.

Amidst macro-level challenges outlined above, our company has all along fared reasonably well and relatively far better than most peers. It should be able to combat current headwinds on the strength of its strong liquidity, sustained improvement in operational efficiencies and overall financial standing.

Moderating Domestic Sugar Demand: domestic sugar consumption is expected to grow at a modest 1.5%–2.0% CAGR over the next five years
Cyclical Nature of the Sugar Industry: influenced by fluctuations in sugar production, inventory levels and market demand
Dependence on Government Policies: relating to sugarcane pricing, export regulations, ethanol procurement prices and other regulatory measures
Climatic and Water Availability Risks: irregular monsoons, reduced river flows, depletion of groundwater resources and low storage levels in reservoirs
Challenges in Adoption of Modern Irrigation: high capital investment, delays in Government subsidy schemes and inadequate water availability during drought years
Emerging Technology Adoption: widespread adoption of AI and precision agriculture expected to take time due to technological, infrastructural and implementation challenges
Commodity price risk is one of the important risks for the Company as commodities form a major part of business.
